t: Inquiry From Police Department, Sydney, New South Wales Re Christian Sander

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. & S. B. REGISTRY
No. D 3863
Date 26/7/32

July 26, 32.

Sir,

Christian Sander

I have the honour to acknowledge receipt of your letter N.P. 6895/2414 of June 21 and, in reply, to state that there is no record of the above named having been prosecuted for any offence in Shanghai, nor is anything known detrimental to his character.

Enquiries show that Sander is an Esthonian subject, about 50 years of age, married to a lady of Russian extraction and has three children. In his youth Sander worked as a telegraph operator in his native country. Some time later he proceeded to Irkutsk, Siberia where he started his own business as a cattle dealer and supplier of dairy produce, in addition to which he opened a pharmacy and a glass factory in the same town.

Following the revolution in Russia in 1917 he devoted his efforts to the repatriation of Esthonian subjects from Russia. When the Bolsheviks came into power he was arrested and imprisoned in Siberia and later in Butyrsky in Moscow. After being incarcerated for about a year he was released during an exchange of prisoners between Esthonia and the U.S.S.R.

1932年7月26日。

先生，

克里斯蒂安·桑德 (Christian Sander)

谨此确认收到阁下于6月21日发出的第 N.P. 6895/2414 号来函，并回复如下：上述人士在上海并无因任何罪行被起诉的记录，亦未闻有任何损及其品行之事。

经查，桑德系爱沙尼亚籍臣民，年约五十岁，娶一俄裔女子为妻，育有三名子女。桑德年轻时曾在其祖国担任电报员。此后不久，他前往西伯利亚伊尔库茨克，在那里开始自营牲畜买卖及乳制品供应业务，此外还在该镇开设了一家药店和一家玻璃厂。

1917年俄国革命后，他致力于协助爱沙尼亚籍臣民从俄国遣返。布尔什维克掌权后，他被捕并先被囚禁于西伯利亚，后被关押于莫斯科的布特尔卡监狱 (Butyrsky)。在被监禁约一年后，他在爱沙尼亚与苏联交换战俘期间获释。

In 1921 Sander arrived in Harbin from Estonia,
via Suez, travelling on a diplomatic passport as a
delegate of the Estonian Republic to negotiate with the
Government of the "Far Eastern Republic". The negotia-
tions however were unsuccessful.

Sander arrived in Shanghai in the early part of
1923 and established a dairy produce business at No. 85
Baikal Road and also opened a grocery store in the
Hongkew Market. He operated these concerns until
November 1923 when he sold his business to a Latvian
named Melbard and departed for Australia, accompanied
by his family.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your obedient servant,

(Sd) K. M. Bourne,
Deputy Commissioner (Crime).

Commissioner of Police,
Sydney,
New South Wales,
Australia.

1921年，桑德从爱沙尼亚经苏伊士抵达哈尔滨，持外交护照作为爱沙尼亚共和国代表，与“远东共和国”政府进行谈判。然而，谈判并未成功。

桑德于1923年初抵达上海，在贝加尔路85号建立了一家乳制品商行，并在虹口市场开设了一家杂货店。他经营这些生意直至1923年11月，随后将业务出售给一名名为梅尔巴德 (Melbard) 的拉脱维亚人，并携家人前往澳大利亚。

谨此致意，
先生，
您顺从的仆人，

（签名）K. M. 伯恩 (K. M. Bourne)，
副总监（刑事）。

警察总监，
悉尼，
新南威尔士州，
澳大利亚。

Made by D.S. Tcheremshansky. Forwarded by [Signature]

With reference to the letter of June 21, 1932, from
the Commissioner of Police, Sydney, New South Wales, requesting
information regarding one Christian Sander, inquiries show that
this individual is an Esthonian subject of about 50 years of age.
In his youth he worked in his native country as a telegraph
operator. In this capacity he worked for some time after which
he proceeded to Irkutsk, Siberia where he started his own
business as a cattle dealer and supplier of dairy produce.
Owing to the prosperous nature of his business he was looked
upon as being a wealthy man. In addition to his farming
projects he opened in Irkutsk a milk shop, a pharmacy and a
glass factory.

Following the revolution of 1917 he devoted his efforts
towards the repatriation Esthonian subjects from Russia, and
when the Bolsheviks came into power he was arrested and
imprisoned first in Siberia and later in Butyrsky prison in
Moscow. After being incarcerated for more than a year he
was released during an exchange of prisoners between Esthonia
and the U.S.S.R.

During 1921 Sander arrived in Harbin from Esthonia
via Suez travelling on a diplomatic passport, as a delegate of
the Esthonian Republic to negotiate with the Government of

subjects. These negotiations however, failed to fructify
after which Sander went to Shanghai, arriving there during the
early part of 1923. In this city he established a dairy produce
business at No. 85 Baikal Road, and at the same time opened

Dear Sir,

I am desirous of obtaining information with
regard to a man named Christian Sander, formerly Zander,
a Russian or Lett, who was until recently Managing Director
of Sanders Limited at Taree in this State. Sander is
described as about fifty years of age, about five feet ten
inches in height, fair hair, blue eyes, fair complexion,
clean shaven, inclined to stoutness, of a genial disposition
and a ready talker.

I have been informed that this man was committed
for trial for making counterfeit coins in Shang-hai in 1924
and absconded from bail.

I would be very glad if you would furnish me
with any information in your possession respecting the man
Sander and particulars of any convictions recorded against
him.

Yours faithfully,

W. H. Childs
Commissioner of Police.

尊敬的先生，

本人希望获取关于一名名叫克里斯蒂安·桑德 (Christian Sander)、原名赞德 (Zander) 的男子的信息，其为俄罗斯人或拉脱维亚人，直至最近一直担任本州塔里 (Taree) 桑德斯有限公司 (Sanders Limited) 的董事总经理。据描述，桑德年约五十岁，身高约五英尺十英寸，金发，蓝眼，肤色白皙，面部无须，体型偏胖，性情和蔼，健谈。

本人获悉，此人曾于1924年在上海因制造假币罪被交付审判，并在保释期间潜逃。

如蒙阁下提供所掌握的关于桑德先生的任何信息，以及针对他的任何定罪记录的详情，本人将不胜感激。

此致，

W. H. 蔡尔兹 (W. H. Childs)
警察总监。
